# Content Calendar App

## Summary
A solo creator's multi-platform content plan in one card — a month calendar
of everything scheduled, bundles that group a video with the posts promoting
it, an idea backlog, recurring series, a bench of freelancers work gets handed to,
and a Rhythm view of posting consistency. Built as a stage-2 POC at `content-calendar/content-calendar.gts`
to prove the Calendar / Contact / Tag cluster composes for a single-operator
app, where the team-shaped concepts (Team, Role, workload) do not apply.

## Composition
- **Cards**: ContentPiece is the atomic unit; ContentBundle groups an anchor plus supporting pieces and computes its own completion; ContentIdea is the unscheduled backlog; ContentSeries carries a cadence; Freelancer extends Contact with specialties and a rate note. Event is consumed unchanged as what a bundle promotes.
- **Fields**: Platform and Content Status are option sets, not raw strings — their hues resolve through `stateColor`, so a linked Theme reskins every chip and no brand colour is reproduced as a literal.
- **Components**: the month Calendar (drag-to-reschedule, kind→colour chips, day overflow, create affordance), StatePill for every state label, EnumSelect for the platform filter. All consumed unchanged.
- **Upstream**: Calendar gained an optional `onExternalDrop` arg. It could previously only accept drops that began on one of its own chips, so there was no way to drag an unscheduled item in from a backlog elsewhere on the page. Additive — the Talent & Resource Tracker is unaffected.
- **Chrome**: `TabbedHeader` carries the six tabs, the app mark as its `headerIcon` and the stat tiles as `sideContent`; `ProgressBar` renders bundle completion. Raw markup where the library has the primitive is a component-discovery fail, so the hand-rolled nav and text-pill progress were replaced.
- **Theming**: the linked Ritmo Studio theme supplies warm paper, plum ink, one hot-magenta accent and a display/text face pairing. Every colour resolves through a semantic token with a `--boxel-*` fallback; the console root declares `--studio-band` as an adapter and never overrides a block's internals. Audited clean: no literals, none hiding in fallbacks, no surface token carrying text, no `@import`, every `color-mix` in oklch toward a token.
- **The hero**: the Rhythm tab is a per-platform sequencer of the month — a filled beat is published, an outlined one planned — with the current streak at display scale. Streaks count days holding a published piece and tolerate a today that isn't over yet, so work in progress doesn't read as a broken run.

## Example
The linked instance is a solo Zumba instructor's world: two months of
real-shaped content across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and Facebook, two
recurring series, six captured ideas, two bundles (one shipped, one in
flight) and a two-person bench.

## Non-goals
Auto-publishing, analytics and payments are out of scope by design — this
tracks, it never posts. Reminders are excluded for a platform reason rather
than a product one: the matrix Remind block is audited as blocked on three
absent pieces (an identity concept, a card-reachable scheduler, a
notification channel), so a reminder that cannot notify would mislead the
user. The honest substitute is the handed-to marker plus the waiting-on view.
Team assignment and workload belong to the team edition of the spec.

## Known gaps — the composable tally
What composed: the month Calendar, StatePill, EnumSelect, TabbedHeader,
ProgressBar, Contact (via Freelancer), Event, base Tag, and the Theme pipeline.
What stayed bespoke, and why:

- **The rhythm sequencer.** A month × platform beat grid has no matrix concept —
  the nearest Structures components are Timeline and the charts, and neither is
  this shape. It is the strongest candidate block this app produced.
- **The idea backlog renders as rows**, not the Kanban block: drag-to-schedule
  targets the Calendar rather than a column, so the board affordance did not fit.
  Revisit if the backlog ever gains stages.
- **Recurring occurrences are materialised on demand**, a bounded number at a
  time, because there is no scheduler a card can reach.
- **No status-change Activity feed** is wired yet, despite one-click status being
  the app's most frequent mutation — the obvious next consumer of Activity.

Each of these is recorded against its concept in the matrix tracker rather than
left as quiet hand-rolled code.
